character_facts: Othon is portrayed as both cunning and extremely lethal in battle.
Bari is physically disabled and cannot use his legs at this stage of the story.
Othon survives catastrophic injury to his groin and hips but is left unable to father more children.
Othon has already lost a son before the end of the recap sequence, as described in the text.
continuity_links: This page is an explicit recap of prior issues rather than new scene progression.
It sets up the current volume/issue by summarizing Othon and Bari's recent history, their imperial bargain, relocation to Okhar, and Othon's mutilation.
dialogue_meaning: The page functions as an editorial recap summarizing the major events leading into this issue.
It emphasizes Othon's military brilliance and ferocity, Bari's accusation of cowardice, the imperial settlement after the war, and Othon's later mutilation and dynastic loss.
locations: the Castaka fortress or stronghold (mentioned in negotiation)
lore_facts: Epyphite is described as a sacred anti-gravity oil flowing in the heart of planet Marmola.
The conflict centers on control of the epyphite.
The Imperial Couple has authority to negotiate planetary grants and commercial percentages.
Bari has lost the use of his legs before the current story point.
Okhar is described as a fertile planet where Othon and Bari settle.
Bari's horse is said to have been extinct for 20,000 years and genetically recreated by imperial scientists.
For the Metabarons lineage, loss of reproductive capacity is framed as loss of hope for continuing the clan.
plot_events: The page recaps earlier events involving Othon, Baron of Castaka, during a war over the epyphite on Marmola.
Othon cannot save his wife from death during the conflict.
Bari accuses Othon of cowardice after Othon stops him from joining his mother in certain death.
Othon later proves his valor by defeating enemy forces with cunning and personally killing many soldiers with only a dagger.
The Imperial Couple arrives to negotiate with Othon and Bari after the victory.
In exchange for the epyphite, Othon requests a share of sales, a new planet for the Castaka stronghold, and a gift for Bari, who has lost the use of his legs.
The Imperial Couple grants the terms, and Othon and Bari settle on the planet Okhar.
Bari receives a specially created horse.
Thieves steal the horse, and Othon pursues them while mistakenly carrying Bari.
As Othon kills the last bandit, the dying attacker shoots him and destroys his groin and hips.
Othon is taken back to be healed, but his servants cannot restore his sexual organs, ending his hope of continuing the clan through a son.
uncertainties: The dense recap text is small and partially low-contrast, so some wording may be imprecise even though the overall events are legible.
The painted figures and circular portraits are not individually labeled on the page, so exact identification of each pictured face is uncertain from this page alone.
visual_summary: A title and recap page for The Metabarons. The page is dominated by the series logo, a block of recap text headed 'Previously,' and painted character art at left showing a grim, damaged warrior figure holding or looming over a bloodied body. Small circular portraits of several faces line the lower middle, and publication credits fill a black band at the bottom.
